stages.title: Foundations
stages.description: Why healthcare is economically unusual and how patients respond to prices, time costs and insurance.

stages.title: Health & behaviour
stages.description: Health capital, investment, socioeconomic gradients and the mechanisms behind disparities.

stages.title: Providers & insurance
stages.description: Physician agency and the insurance problems that complete the health-economics framework.

sessions.title: Health Economics and the Healthcare Economy
sessions.summary: Why healthcare matters economically, why its markets are unusual, and how patients, providers and payers fit together.

sessions.title: Healthcare Demand
sessions.summary: Demand curves, elasticity, RAND and Oregon, time costs, and how insurance changes the price patients face.

sessions.title: Health Capital and the Demand for Health
sessions.summary: The Grossman model: health as capital, depreciation, productive time, the MEC and comparative statics.

sessions.title: Socio-economic Disparities in Health
sessions.summary: Direct causality, reverse causality and third-factor explanations for socioeconomic health gradients.

sessions.title: Physician Agency
sessions.summary: Principal–agent problems, physician-induced demand, payment incentives and small-area practice variation.

sessions.title: Insurance 1: Demand for Healthcare Insurance
sessions.summary: Risk, demand and supply of insurance, full versus partial coverage, and fair versus unfair contracts.

sessions.title: Insurance 2: Adverse Selection & the Role of Government
sessions.summary: Adverse selection, plan competition, pooling and separating equilibria, renewability and public intervention.

sessions.title: Insurance 3: Moral Hazard
sessions.summary: Demand-side and supply-side cost sharing, moral hazard, value-based insurance and managed care.
